items.stem: What is a Segment in a Synnduit Run?

options.text: One step inside a Run — either a Migration or a GarbageCollection on one entity type

items.explanation: A Run is an ordered list of Segments; each Segment is one step (Migration or GarbageCollection) on one entity type.

misconceptions.b: That's the Run; a Segment is one step within it.

items.stem: Which Segment type removes / cleans up destination records whose source record has disappeared?
items.explanation: GarbageCollection handles destination records that no longer have a corresponding source record. Migration pushes creates/updates in.

misconceptions.a: Migration adds and updates; it does not handle source-disappeared cleanup.

items.stem: For migrating in (School is the parent, Student references School, StudentAddress references Student), put the Migration segments in the correct order.
items.explanation: Migrate parents before children: School, then Student, then StudentAddress — so each child can reference a parent that already exists.

items.stem: Why do you migrate School before Student, but garbage-collect Student before School?
rubric: Migration order: parents first so children can reference an existing parent (no missing foreign key)
GC order: children first (reverse) so you don't delete a parent while children still reference it (no orphaned/violated foreign key)
items.sampleAnswer: Migrating adds records, so the parent (School) must exist before a child (Student) can reference it. Garbage collection deletes records, so you must remove the children (Students) first; deleting a School while Students still point to it would violate the foreign key.

items.stem: How is a Run launched at CCSD, and what does the GUID in the command do?

options.text: Synnduit <RunName> <RunGuid>; the GUID identifies the run in StarBridge so history stays consistent across executions
Synnduit <RunName>; the GUID is a license key
It is started from the dashboard; the GUID is the user's ID
Synnduit <RunGuid>; the GUID is generated fresh each run

items.explanation: Runs are CLI invocations of the form 'Synnduit <RunName> <RunGuid>'. The GUID ties the run to its StarBridge history so identity is stable across executions.

misconceptions.d: A fresh GUID each run would break history continuity; the GUID is stable per run.
